title: feat(app-shell)!: ObjectView's props are the declared ConsoleObjectViewProps, not any (objectui#7483)
body:
Fixes #7483
Clause-②: yes — a published component's props type narrows from `any` to a declared interface.
Ruling-ref: 5809238375 (UI closure batch 2 item 9, letter declare) and 5871194128 (batch 238 item 1, letter B, maintainer 「同意」 2026-09-28T13:47Z)

**Fix round 1** (`a527bc95ae`), following contract review `5874389538`:
- `_PropsAreTheRuledShape` pins `ConsoleObjectViewProps` to the ruled shape (names, optionality, value types). It is red with TS2344 under `onEdit?:` and under `objects?:`, and green at head.
- The changeset sentence about which mounts compile now states the `strictFunctionTypes` consequence for `onEdit` and the number type of `externalRefreshKey`.

`Bundle Analysis` is red because `main` itself is over the eager-closure ceiling (objectui#10996; standing-down comment `5874286944`). It is not a required check.
Follow-up from the review: the customer skill guide's broken `ObjectView` mount is objectui#11011.

Claim: 5873302545 · executed by the `domain:ui` seat 2 dispatch, session `https://claude.ai/code/session_014mXUNuFomfj24w7s1pZzhN` (mode:subagent). Base `8aa68b1596`, head `f5cf7121d3`.

## What changed

- `@object-ui/app-shell`'s `ObjectView` and its inner body `ObjectViewInner` no longer take a bare `any`. Both are typed with the new exported `ConsoleObjectViewProps`, with exactly the ruled members:
  - `dataSource: DataSource` (the published `@object-ui/types` contract), required;
  - `objects: any[]`, required and kept loose (the object-metadata type prices at 75 diagnostics and is out of this card);
  - `onEdit`, a function taking a Record of string to unknown and returning void, required;
  - `externalRefreshKey?: number`.
- `ConsoleObjectViewProps` is re-exported as a type from the package entry, beside `RecordFormPageProps`, through the views barrel. It is not named `ObjectViewProps`: `@object-ui/plugin-view` owns that name for a different shape (objectui#6172, one authority per exported type name). plugin-view is untouched (0-line diff under `packages/plugin-view`).
- `packages/app-shell/README.md`: the `### ObjectView` block now passes the four props and lists them. The old block mounted the view with `dataSource` alone. It compiled, and a verbatim copy threw on first render at `objects.find(...)`.
- Changeset `7483-console-objectview-props.md`, `'@object-ui/app-shell': minor`. It states the narrowing: the props type is declared, `onEdit` and `objects` are now required at the type level, and a misspelled prop is a compile error.

Nothing changes at runtime except the two bytes of one optional call, listed next.

## Diagnostics raised by the typed `dataSource`, each repaired by typing

Re-measured on today's main: 3. That matches the earlier dev report's V6 count (comment 5828686918). There is no cast to `any` and no `@ts-expect-error`.

1. **TS2722**, "Cannot invoke an object which is possibly 'undefined'". This is the debounced `dataSource.updateViewConfig(...)` call inside the `setTimeout` closure of `persistViewPatch`. The guard at the top of the callback does not narrow into the closure, and the contract declares `updateViewConfig` optional. **Repair:** an optional member call, `dataSource.updateViewConfig?.(...)`, which keeps the adapter as `this`.
2. **TS2559**, "Type 'DataSource of any' has no properties in common with type 'Partial of ViewCacheInvalidator'". This is at the view-config save's `persistRuntimeMetadata('view', ...)` call.
3. **TS2559**, the same message, at the create-view flow's `createRuntimeMetadata('view', ...)` call.

**Repair for 2 and 3:** the seam declares the capability it probes. `RuntimePersistCtx.dataSource` in `runtime-metadata-persistence.ts` was a bare Partial of `ViewCacheInvalidator`, which is a weak type (every member optional). The published `DataSource` does not declare `invalidateViewKeys`; only the `ObjectStackAdapter` class does. So TypeScript refused a typed `DataSource`.

The seam is now declared as what it really takes: the host's adapter object, probed for that one capability. It is written as the intersection of `object` and a Partial of `ViewCacheInvalidator`, or null. That still refuses a primitive and a wrongly typed `invalidateViewKeys`, which was probed in isolation before the edit. It admits the partial test doubles the seam's own suites pass. The type is not reachable from the package entry: `RuntimePersistCtx`, `ViewCacheInvalidator` and the module name have 0 hits in the built `dist/index.d.ts`.

The optional call changes the source text a source-level ratchet reads. The objectui#5233 ratchet test (`the toolbar write routes its body through buildPersistedViewBody` in `ObjectView.overlayPatchOnly.test.ts`) located the call site by the literal `dataSource.updateViewConfig(`. Its vacuous-pass guard fired, 1 failed. Its pattern now accepts both spellings of the same call and its guard is unchanged: 17/17 green.

## Pins: red on base, green on head

`ObjectView.consoleProps.types.test.tsx` sits beside the view and is compiled by app-shell's `tsconfig.test.json`. `--listFiles` shows it and `ObjectView.tsx` among that project's inputs. It is `.tsx` rather than `.ts` because the refusals are JSX mounts; the precedent is `InspectorComboField.naming.types.test.tsx`. Its rows:

- the misspelled prop `dataSourceX` is **TS2322**;
- a mount that omits `objects` and `onEdit` is **TS2739** ("missing the following properties from type 'ConsoleObjectViewProps': objects, onEdit");
- the four-prop control compiles;
- type equations: the parameter is not `any`, the parameter equals `ConsoleObjectViewProps`, and `dataSource` equals `DataSource`.

The two codes were read from a directive-free copy of the file, which was removed after the read.

| leg | what was on disk | `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **base** (base `ObjectView.tsx` checked out, restored after) | parameter `any`, no interface | exit 2: TS2305 (no exported member `ConsoleObjectViewProps`), TS2344 on `_ParamNotAny`, TS2344 on `_DataSourceIsTheContract`, **TS2578 on both `@ts-expect-error` directives** |
| **mutation** (head, only the exported parameter set back to `any`, via `ablation-replace.mjs`) | interface present, parameter `any` | exit 2: TS2344 on `_ParamNotAny`, TS2344 on `_ParamIsTheDeclaredProps`, **TS2578 on both directives** |
| **head** `f5cf7121d3` | as committed | exit 0 (inside `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check`, VERDICT command-exit 0) |

Restore after both red legs was proven by blob and diff: the `ObjectView.tsx` blob equals the HEAD blob `fe60b6d70fcd`, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

The runtime half is `vitest run` of the pin: 3/3 passed. The elements are created, never rendered.

**README block now checks something.** A planted `dataSourceX` in the README's `ObjectView` block turns `pnpm check:doc-snippets` red: exit 1, "679 of 679 block(s) judged, 1 failed", TS2322 "Property 'dataSourceX' does not exist". The restore was proven by blob. The card measured the same mutation green on the old block.

**One-authority gate control.** The gate is `scripts/__tests__/one-authority-per-exported-name-6273.test.ts`. Under `ConsoleObjectViewProps` it exits 0 with 11 passed (11). Under the originally ruled name `ObjectViewProps`, as a mutation that was restored, it exits 1 on "ObjectViewProps — a NEW colliding name". `ConsoleObjectViewProps` had 0 hits on main before this change.

## Gates (at head `f5cf7121d3` unless stated)

- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell build`: exit 0; `dist` carries `ConsoleObjectViewProps` in `index.d.ts` and `views/ObjectView.d.ts`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check`, both `tsc --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`: VERDICT command-exit 0. The base measurement was 0 and 0.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console type-check`, with the console dependency closure built first: VERDICT command-exit 0.
- Tests: `pnpm exec vitest run` over 84 files, reported as "Test Files 84 passed (84), Tests 2108 passed (2108)". The 84 files are:
  - every file that imports app-shell's `views/ObjectView`, including the three console suites that mock it;
  - every test that reads `ObjectView.tsx` by path;
  - every importer of `runtime-metadata-persistence`;
  - the new pin.
- In-repo callers: git grep finds exactly two mounts of app-shell's `ObjectView`, both in `AppContent`, and both pass all four props. The `ObjectView` mounted in `examples/byo-backend-console` and in the console's timeline test is plugin-view's, imported from `@object-ui/plugin-view`. No caller needed a change.
- One-authority gate: exit 0, 11/11 (see above).
- `pnpm check:doc-snippets`: exit 0, "Semantic phase: 679 of 679 block(s) judged, 0 failed". It was first run before the scoped build it asks for and answered PRECONDITION NOT MET (exit 2); that run is not a measurement.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: exit 0. It reports "6 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)".
- `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`: exit 0.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-fixed.mjs`: exit 0.
- `pnpm check:changeset-claims`: exit 0 (report-only). It names three pending changesets that cite files this change touches: `6238-object-payload-enabled.md`, `6559-expression-user-input-contract.md` and `7070-no-invented-gantt-date-fields.md`. Each paragraph was re-read and is still true.
- `pnpm check:pending-changeset-literals`: exit 0.
- `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: "0 new citation(s)", exit 0.
- `pnpm check:control-bytes`: exit 0.
- `check:readme-exports`, `check:doc-fences`, `check:doc-examples`, `check:docs-route-closure`, `check:icon-record-names`, `check:i18n-keys` and `check:handler-key-reads`: each exit 0. These are the gates that read the README or `ObjectView.tsx`.
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the 8 changed paths: NOT GOVERNED.
- Targeted lint: `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 6 changed ts/tsx files reported 6 files, 0 errors. The population is `eslint.config.js`, which has no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`, so the linting is not type-aware and the diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file. `ObjectView.tsx` warnings went from 172 to 171. The full `pnpm lint` is owned by CI.
- `git merge-tree --write-tree`: clean against a fresh main `d6d8fb9d7b` and clean against the head of PR objectui#10990, `d3747ac005`, which also edits the entry. The merged entry keeps both additions.
- `pnpm check:eager-closure`: **exit 1, and exit 1 on the base too.** The local console build reads **3,179,021** gzipped bytes at head against a base of **3,179,020**. The base was measured with the four base app-shell sources on disk, then restored. The budget is 3,179,000 bytes. So main is already 20 bytes over in this container, and this PR adds **+1 gzip byte (+2 raw)**, the `?.` of the optional call. The dispatch's 3104.0 KB reading does not reproduce on today's main. On CI, `Bundle Analysis` on main is `failure` at `6650259081` and `d6d8fb9d7b`, failing at step "Check console performance budget", and `cancelled` at this PR's base.

## Acceptance notes

- `ObjectViewInner` is not exported, so the pin cannot reach it. Its typing is judged by the `src` leg only, through the one forwarding mount inside `ObjectView`. Setting only the inner parameter back to `any` would not turn the pin red.
- The claim's file surface did not name three of the touched files; each is a direct consequence of the ruled repairs:
  - `runtime-metadata-persistence.ts`, where the seam's declaration lives;
  - `views/index.ts`, the barrel the entry re-exports through;
  - `ObjectView.overlayPatchOnly.test.ts`, the ratchet pattern.
- `content/docs/guide/console-architecture.md` describes app-shell's `ObjectView` as a wrapper but names no props, so it is not edited.
- The eager-closure red is pre-existing on main, as the reading above shows. This PR's `Bundle Analysis` is expected to be red for that reason until main's budget or closure moves.
